plainSummary: Saved tests can be inspected and rerun while stale inputs, unsafe paths and uncertain retries stay guarded.
summary: Independent review of final saved-check worker, shared application/CLI/MCP interfaces, narrow local bridge, metadata and UI. Executed 20 core adversarial tests (including eight new saved-check killers) and three rendered/UI interaction tests. Former evidence/runs symlink escape reproduced red, then same unchanged killer passed after all destination ancestors were confined before dispatch and final writes. Source changes during execution produce missing; stale displayed input rejects before worker; overlapping requests reject while same request reuses identity; 200KB stdout/stderr are drained with32KiB captures and integrity hashes; nonzero exit retains diagnostics; actual worker timeout/SIGKILL path confirms owned command termination before guard release (only120000ms timer compressed75ms). Local invalid origin/token/private cwd/oversize requests cause no run. UI source/log text escapes markup and uncertain409 reconnect retains request identity. Reviewed retry previousRunId and capturedBytes provenance. Repaired prior collector killer to wait for observed owned-process exit rather than assume150ms, preserving host survival and emitfalse assertions. Root reports production UI build/typecheck passed; final broad suite and explicit claim run are still pending and are not claimed by this review.

residualRisks: Saved repository shell commands execute with host privileges; this feature is not a sandbox for malicious repository code.
Ambiguous worker termination intentionally retains its execution guard and does not silently retry.
Timeout test compresses only the timer duration while exercising real subprocess termination; it is not a120-second wall-clock soak.
Historical discarded logs cannot be reconstructed; authored inputs/expectations remain descriptions rather than reporter-produced assertion results.
